subject: TTFT & streaming SLOs — post-call recap and next steps
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@finapps.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Feb 2026 15:10:00 -0800
Subject: TTFT & streaming SLOs — post-call recap and next steps

Alex — great talk earlier, thanks for the time. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on performance targets and what Redwood can validate during a short tech deep-dive.

1) Goals you stated on the call
- Time-to-first-token (TTFT): target <= 150 ms for short prompts (50–200 tokens) on production traffic
- Streaming: SSE or WebSocket streaming for incremental tokens; target chunk cadence <= 200 ms between chunks for real-time UX
- Throughput / concurrency: sustained ~200 requests/sec average across region with bursts to ~500 rps; typical concurrency 40–80 per model; peak concurrency for spikes up to 120

2) Clarifications / assumptions from our side
- TTFT is highly dependent on model size and deployment mode (hosted vs dedicated). We'll validate on the model(s) you plan to use.
- Network and client-side buffering affect observed chunk cadence — we'll factor that into tests.

3) Immediate next steps (proposed)
- You: share representative prompt set + example payloads (JSONL) and an estimate of % streaming clients (you mentioned ~70% streaming).
- Us: run a short perf harness (server-side + streaming) against your representative payloads and share a small benchmark report and recommended config (batching, concurrency, cache settings).
- Schedule: propose a 45m technical deep-dive with Marissa (solutions) and Lauren (platform) — we have availability Thurs 26 Feb 10:00–11:00 PT.

4) Acceptance criteria suggestions (we can customize)
- TTFT: median <= 150ms, 95th <= 350ms for target model;
- Chunk cadence: median inter-chunk <= 200ms for first N chunks;
- Error budget: error rate < 0.5% for streaming sessions over a 24h window.

I attached a lightweight SLO template and an example payload file to make it easier for your team to provide inputs. If you confirm the sample payloads, Marissa will run the initial tuning and perf run.

Thanks — looking forward to the deep-dive.

—
Aditya Rao
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com | (415) 555-0147
From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@finapps.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Samira Patel <samira.p@finapps.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Feb 2026 09:14:23 -0800
Subject: Re: TTFT & streaming SLOs — post-call recap and next steps

Aditya — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming a few things and adding detail from our side:

- We prefer WebSocket streaming for our mobile clients (lower overhead for many open connections), but SSE is fine for server-to-server flows. Expect ~70% of traffic to be streaming.
- Average request payload: ~800–1,200 bytes (mostly short prompts + metadata).
- Typical QPS: baseline ~180 rps, peak bursts up to ~480 rps; typical sustained concurrency around 60, but spikes can push to ~120 concurrent streaming sessions.
- Our ideal TTFT target would be 100 ms for short prompts (if achievable) — can you call out what that looks like across hosted vs dedicated?

We will upload a representative sample of prompts and an anonymized client trace from our staging traffic (will include chunk timestamps) — I can get that to you by EOD Wednesday. Also appreciate any benchmark artifacts or a one-page runbook describing what Redwood will measure during the perf run.

If Thurs 26th 10am PT works for Marissa and Lauren, that is good for us.

Alex
Product Lead, Integrations
FinApps
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@finapps.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Feb 2026 13:30:06 -0800
Subject: Re: TTFT & streaming SLOs — post-call recap and next steps

Alex — thanks, great context. A few technical notes ahead of the Fri deep-dive (so you know what we'll validate and what to expect):

Quick TL;DR:
- WebSocket is preferred for large numbers of long-lived streaming clients; SSE is simpler but has higher per-connection overhead across proxies.
- TTFT 100 ms is an aggressive target and is model+deployment dependent. On Redwood Dedicated with a quantized 13B model and optimized kernels we typically see median TTFT in the 100–140 ms range for short prompts; hosted multi-tenant depends on fleet contention and often runs ~150–250 ms.
- Chunk cadence (first 3 chunks): user-level 100–200 ms is achievable with the right batching + small generation steps; network and client buffers can add ~10–50 ms.

What we'll measure in the perf run:
- Cold vs warm TTFT (first request after either model load / cache miss vs subsequent requests)
- Median/95/99 latency for first token and per-chunk inter-arrival times
- Throughput shaping and backpressure behavior at target concurrency (we'll simulate 200 rps steady + 500 rps bursts)
- Connection scaling (open WebSocket connections and per-connection memory)

Questions / asks for your team
- Please send a sample JSONL of prompts (one-per-line) and an example of the expected response size distribution (we need this to choose generation chunk sizes).
- If you can share a small staging trace with chunk timestamps that will help us match chunk cadence objectives during testing.

Recommended initial config for the perf run (we can tune after initial results):
- Deployment: Redwood Dedicated (24/7 reserved capacity) for lowest variance
- Concurrency target: 100 concurrent streams; stress to 150 for spike tests
- Batching: micro-batching at 10ms windows for high qps; prefix caching enabled for repeated prompts
- Protocol: WebSocket for mobile; SSE for server-to-server

I attached an example payload file and a short SLO template you can review. We'll also prepare a short benchmark summary after the run and propose specific quantization / batching settings.

See you Thurs 26 Feb 10:00 PT — joining info in the calendar invite (sent by Aditya).

Best,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
